analysis_kind: Exploratory parent-only analyzer diagnostic; not a cohort evaluation or independent truth labeling.
hypothesis: Module-level unresolved dependencies may activate global behavior fallback across real parent graphs, independently of already known-incomplete provenance. Measure prevalence without assuming it or changing policy.
method: Use the 63 frozen parent groups and exact claims/provenance/draft hashes from the referenced inventory.
Read only each parent tree with existing source_roots and build the production Python graph; retain graph hash and source blob identity for every indexed module.
Record modules, definitions, edges, limitations, unresolved nodes, and global_unresolved; distinguish module unresolved flags already present after parsing from flags added while linking imports.
For all 630 candidate subjects record definition presence, ambiguity, direct unresolved flag, module unresolved flag and graph global flag. Aggregate behavior candidates separately.
Compare warm-cache and fresh indexes for every parent; do not time or benchmark this run.
Store complete parent graph views and per-module facts, not only aggregates.
limits: Parent graphs are not transitions; prevalence does not establish actual child validation frequency or achievable speedup.
No source-level unresolved marker is interpreted as a truth label or proof of a missing runtime dependency.
All original known_incomplete markers remain intact; no provenance, receipts, labels, closure or admission is created.
No child commits, held-out outcomes, probes, policy execution, or simulated supported MemoryStates are used.
The diagnostic uses the CAMI analyzer and is not an independent extraction-quality evaluation.
